requirements.requirement: Configure the opsadmin account on node1 with the specified SSH public key.
requirements.summary: The account was created with a home directory, and the exact requested ED25519 key was installed in authorized_keys with opsadmin ownership and restrictive permissions. These properties remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication for opsadmin.
requirements.summary: The effective per-user sshd policy enables public-key authentication, requires AuthenticationMethods publickey, and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. sshd configuration validation succeeded, the service remained active and reachable, and the policy persisted after restart.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also well evidenced: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was scheduled and observed through transient disconnection, the boot ID changed from 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a to a054e14a-0b8c-48fb-b4cd-252b3e17b166, and the recovered node retained its account, key, SSH policy, service health, and reachability. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No end-to-end SSH login was attempted with the corresponding private key. Access is therefore established through coherent account, exact-key, permissions, effective-policy, service-health, and reachability observations rather than a completed authenticated session.

The restart command reported that reboot was scheduled rather than returning a separate provider acknowledgement; subsequent connection loss, changed boot identity, healthy recovery, and lifecycle observations directly confirm that the restart occurred.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating and unlocking opsadmin, installing its key, applying the key-only policy, reloading sshd, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were identified. The sole hygiene defect is the retained /tmp/harbor-reboot.log created by the restart command; it is minor executor residue and was not cleaned up. No failed services, damaged package state, or new network exposure was observed.
